title: The FRIENDS group chat decides who you are
dek: The coffee shop, the rent, the 2am voice notes. Twelve questions about how you behave in a group of six, and which of them you actually are.

questions.prompt: The coffee shop closes in ten minutes and nobody at the table has moved.

options.label: Order one more and start a new topic
Stack the cups and mention the time
Stay until they turn the lights off
Be the one who says 'we should do this more'

questions.prompt: One free table. Three friends are at it. The person from work you've been avoiding just walked in.

options.label: Sit with the friends. Wave at the work person
Merge the tables. Chaos is a social skill
Order to go and text from outside
Sit with the work person. Ask about their weekend

questions.prompt: The flat comes with one impossible thing:

options.label: A fridge that never runs out
A door to every place you've lived

questions.prompt: The best friendships survive living together.
I say 'five minutes away' before I've found my shoes.
There's a note on the fridge: 'I know what you did.' It's in your handwriting.

options.label: Add 'and I'd do it again'
Interrogate everyone separately
Ignore it. It's a bit
Rewrite it in someone else's handwriting

questions.prompt: A friend's partner being wrong is not my problem.
Pick the door you'd knock on at midnight.

options.label: Cottage door, paint coming off
options.alt: An old cottage door with peeling paint

options.label: Long hallway, one light on
options.alt: A dim apartment hallway with one lit door

options.label: Brass knocker, obviously inherited
options.alt: An ornate door with a brass knocker

options.label: Yellow door under a streetlight
options.alt: A yellow front door lit by a streetlight

questions.prompt: Your parents ask when the 'proper job' is happening.

options.label: Say it's going great. It isn't
Explain the whole plan, with slides
Ask them to define 'proper'
Change the subject to food

questions.prompt: I have a story that is 90% true and 10% better.
questions.high: It gets a laugh every time

questions.prompt: I'd rather organise the trip than enjoy it.
Everyone is late and the table is under your name.

options.label: Take it and order for everyone
Give the name as someone else's
Wait outside and narrate arrivals
Order starters and call it dinner

results.name: Rachel Green
results.blurb: You arrive late, look great, and somehow leave with the thing everyone wanted. Your instincts are better than your planning, which is why you keep getting away with it. You're also the friend who says the encouraging thing at exactly the moment it's needed — even if you're texting it from a taxi you can't afford.
strengths: Genuinely good at hyping other people
results.watchOut: Not everything is a plot point. Sometimes the answer is just 'I'm sorry, I'll be there.'

results.name: Monica Geller
results.tagline: Has a system and a spare system
results.blurb: You are the load-bearing wall of your friend group. You host, you plan, you notice who hasn't eaten, and you have opinions about how the dishwasher should be loaded. Your standards are high because you care, not because you're difficult — although it can look like both.
strengths: Makes a room feel looked after
Turns a vague plan into an actual evening
Notices the one person who's gone quiet
results.watchOut: You're allowed to be a guest sometimes. Let someone else burn the dinner.

results.name: Chandler Bing
results.blurb: You are the funniest person in the chat and the last to say what's actually wrong. Humour is how you hold a room together and how you keep it at arm's length. When you do get sincere, people stop scrolling — because it's rare and it's always accurate.
strengths: Reads subtext better than anyone admits
Loyal in a quiet, unglamorous way
results.watchOut: The joke can be the answer, but it can't be the whole conversation. Say the plain version once.

results.name: Phoebe Buffay
results.tagline: Operating on a frequency you don't have
results.blurb: You live slightly to the left of everyone else and it works for you. You're kind without being sentimental, blunt without being cruel, and completely unbothered by what the group considers normal. People come to you for the answer they weren't expecting.
strengths: Kind in ways nobody asked for
results.watchOut: Independence can turn into distance. Let someone in on the plan occasionally.

results.name: Joey Tribbiani
results.blurb: You are the friend who shows up. Not with a plan or a speech — with food, a terrible idea and total commitment to whatever the group is doing. You don't hold grudges and you don't do subtext, which makes you the easiest person in the room to be around.
strengths: Recovers from anything with a snack
results.watchOut: Being easygoing isn't the same as being fine. Say the awkward thing before it builds.

results.name: Ross Geller
results.blurb: You need the facts to line up. You'll correct the timeline, find the receipt and explain why it matters — and you'll be right, which is not always the same as being helpful. Under the pedantry is someone who cares enormously and is terrified of getting it wrong.
strengths: Remembers the detail that settles it
Will do the unglamorous, correct thing
results.watchOut: Being right is not a love language. Ask what they need before you explain.
